Bit size of a pedigree

Source: R/bitSize.R
bitSize.Rd

The bit size of a pedigree, 2 * nNonFounder - nFounder: the measure shrinkPedigree reduces toward its maxBits budget, and its first bitSize value. A founder is an animal whose sire and dam are both unknown (NA); an animal with one known parent is a non-founder (see isFounder).

Usage

bitSize(ped)

Arguments

ped

a pedigree data.frame with the fields id, sire and dam.

Value

A list of three integers: bitSize, nFounder and nNonFounder.

Details

It returns the same list as kinship2::bitSize(), from a pedigree data frame instead of a kinship2 pedigree object.

It stops with shrinkPedigree()'s message when ped lacks id, sire or dam (naming them), is not a data frame, has an id that is missing, empty or repeated, has a sire or dam that is not an id of ped, or has an animal that is both a sire and a dam.

References

Sinnwell JP, Therneau TM, Schaid DJ (2014). "The kinship2 R Package for Pedigree Data." Human Heredity, 78(2), 91-93.

See also

shrinkPedigree, findUnavailable, findAvailNonInform, findAvailAffected

Examples

## A, B and E are founders; C, D and F are not
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "D"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
bitSize(ped)
#> $bitSize
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $nFounder
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $nNonFounder
#> [1] 3
#>
